Less expressive? I don’t think anyone’s said it like that to me. My wife says I get that “look” sometimes, but she says that about anything when she thinks I’m not listening.

Same with my fishing stuff—every weekend, somehow, something gets spoiled or messed with, and then I’m supposed to believe it’s all just a coincidence. I used to fish with a guy from work, back when the plant had a different shift schedule, and we never had this kind of nonsense.\n\nIt’s been months now, and it’s plain to me he’s trying to take over my place, push me out. That’s why I’m here, because apparently I have to explain what’s right in front of everybody.\n\nDoctor: Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?\n\nPatient: Voices? No, not like… I don’t sit there hearing somebody talking when nobody’s around, if that’s what you mean. It’s more that things happen and people act like I’m supposed to ignore it.\n\nLike, I’ll be in the garage and I know where I left something, because I’ve had the same routine for years—work, come home, put things where they go—and then it’s not there. And then my wife says I must’ve moved it, but that’s just… no. But voices, no, I haven’t noticed anything like that.\n\nDoctor: When these things happen, have you been drinking heavily?\n\nPatient: Drinking heavily? I mean… no, I don’t think so. I’ll have a drink here and there, like anybody, but that’s not what this is about.\n\nPeople keep trying to make it into something I’m doing wrong, you know? Like if they can point to a beer or something, then suddenly my tools didn’t get moved and my stuff didn’t get messed with. I worked in that plant for years, and you don’t keep a job like that if you’re stumbling around all the time. So… no, I haven’t noticed heavy drinking being part of it.\n\nDoctor: Have you felt that someone can put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?\n\nPatient: Put thoughts in my mind? I don’t… I don’t think of it like that. My thoughts are my thoughts, as far as I can tell.\n\nNow, people can get in your head in the sense that they keep pushing and pushing, you know? Like at work, back when I was on the line, a supervisor could say one little thing and it’d stick with you all day. But actually putting thoughts in there or taking them out—no, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I just know what’s happening around me, and that’s the part people keep trying to make fuzzy.\n\nDoctor: Have you seen things that other people could not see?\n\nPatient: Seen things? I mean… not like a person standing there that nobody else sees, if that’s what you’re getting at. I don’t think so.\n\nSometimes you catch something out of the corner of your eye, but everybody does that, especially when you’re tired or when the light in the garage is bad. That fluorescent one flickers—been meaning to replace it, but then you go to the store and they don’t even carry the same kind anymore, everything’s changed over to those new bulbs. Anyway… no, I haven’t noticed seeing things other people couldn’t see.\n\nDoctor: About how long have you been convinced that your wife’s relative has been coming into the house and messing with your things?\n\nPatient: About nine months, I’d say. It started right around when my wife’s relative moved into our home. I don’t know… I mean, my wife says I “go on,” but she says that when she doesn’t want to listen, too. People at work used to understand me fine if it was about the job, because with assembly you have to explain things in order—part A, part B, torque this, check that.\n\nSometimes I’ll start explaining something and I have to back up because there’s a reason for it, you know? Like you can’t just say the wrench moved without saying where it was supposed to be, or what shelf, or who had been around. Otherwise people miss the whole point. So… I don’t know if they’d say hard to follow exactly. I haven’t had some big brain thing that I know of.
